newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform on dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform on dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing as a rally in the Canadian dollar after a selloff on Wednesday helped send bond prices higher, analysts said.

"The Canadian dollar definitely was a factor. It retraced quite a bit from its selloff yesterday. Other than that, activity has been pretty light. There hasn't been a lot of flows," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.72 to C$116.52 to yield 6.712 percent.
In other economic news, Statistics Canada reported that retail sales rose a stronger than expected 1.1 percent in April from March. Analysts said the market largely disregarded the data.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.48 to C$108.25 to yield 6.128 percent, while the U.S. 10-year rose 1/32 to yield 6.39 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 26 basis points from 21 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.81 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.07 percent.
